doc.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025

title: The end of an era and training students for gigs
summary: He says he was at the end of an era of working bands, and in Lexington took students on gigs and trained them.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: You know the people after me, except maybe four or five years after me, were still getting jobs with Woody Herman and, you know Buddy Rich and Maynard Ferguson lasted a lot longer. But the young people today, they don’t get to play, really they can play with a pop star if they’re lucky to get a gig with them. And you know they play a few other things, but I mean we were playing all the time: dinner theaters, you know, all kinds of stuff. So you know that’s why it’s important — see I never played in Lexington very much because if I played some of the students couldn’t go out that were ready to go out.
Oh Vince, I never thought of that.
Yeah. And so even the rhythm sec — I never had good rhythm sections. I had to train them so when I did go out it was with the students. And I’d have a short rehearsal, okay
we’re playing a fashion show. Because I said well this is a good gig for them because they’re never going to see one of these for a while.

I said, “Now this is what we’re going to do.” I said, “I’m going to have a list of tunes for you and we’re going to go over them tonight. We’re not going to go over them, I’m going to show you how they go and how we’re going to do it and what you need to do and when you need to stop playing each tune and start playing the next one. So you know we did that and they — you know little blips here and there. I did a dance program with one of those with a jazz dance thing. I said, “Well we’re going to play these tunes and we’re going to rehearse, because we have to rehearse, and you get paid a little money for this.” Usually it was the money I was supposed to get. You know? But it was because that’s part of their education. And Roland Kirk came to town.
